You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Summary of Modifications

The patch modifies a single file, `net/sched/cls_u32.c`, in the `u32_classify()` function. It replaces three calls to `skb_header_pointer()` (which does not fully validate negative `@offset` values) with calls to `skb_header_pointer_careful()` (which does). Additionally, it removes a manual bound check that was no longer needed.

#### Modifications in `net/sched/cls_u32.c`:

1. **First hunk (line 161-164)**:  
   - Removed the check: `if (skb_headroom(skb) + toff > INT_MAX) goto out;`  
   - Changed the call:  
     `skb_header_pointer(skb, toff, 4, &hdata)` → `skb_header_pointer_careful(skb, toff, 4, &hdata)`

2. **Second hunk (line 214-217)**:  
   - Changed the call:  
     `skb_header_pointer(skb, off + n->sel.hoff, 4, &hdata)` → `skb_header_pointer_careful(skb, off + n->sel.hoff, 4, &hdata)`

3. **Third hunk (line 229-232)**:  
   - Changed the call:  
     `skb_header_pointer(skb, off + n->sel.offoff, 2, &hdata)` → `skb_header_pointer_careful(skb, off + n->sel.offoff, 2, &hdata)`

#### Relationships Between Modifications

All three modifications occur in the same function `u32_classify()` and share the same purpose: to safely handle potentially negative offset values when accessing packet data. The first modification also eliminates an earlier insufficient check (`toff > INT_MAX`) because `skb_header_pointer_careful()` now correctly validates negative offsets internally. The changes together close a root cause of a slab-out-of-bounds vulnerability (KASAN report) by ensuring that `skb_header_pointer_careful()` is used consistently in all places where an offset is passed to `skb_header_pointer()`.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>data = skb_header_pointer(skb, toff, 4, &hdata);</text>
<text>data = skb_header_pointer(skb, off + n->sel.hoff, 4, &hdata);</text>
<text>data = skb_header_pointer(skb, off + n->sel.offoff, 2, &hdata);</text>
Reason:
These calls use skb_header_pointer() which does not fully validate negative offset values. When the computed offset (toff, off+hoff, off+offoff) becomes negative, skb_header_pointer() may return a pointer to memory before the skb head, leading to out-of-bounds access (slab-out-of-bounds).

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>data = skb_header_pointer_careful(skb, toff, 4, &hdata);</text>
<text>data = skb_header_pointer_careful(skb, off + n->sel.hoff, 4, &hdata);</text>
<text>data = skb_header_pointer_careful(skb, off + n->sel.offoff, 2, &hdata);</text>
Reason:
skb_header_pointer_careful() properly validates the offset, including negative values, returning NULL for invalid offsets. This prevents the out-of-bounds access by ensuring only valid memory regions are dereferenced.
